= Epistemic Audit Framework: Systematic Knowledge Quality Assessment =

== Executive Summary

This framework provides systematic procedures for auditing BITwiki content epistemic quality. It addresses confidence calibration, source verification, bias detection, and falsification condition assessment.

'''Purpose:''' Ensure all BITwiki content meets epistemic transparency standards and accurately reflects evidence quality.

----
== 1. Audit Dimensions

=== 1.1 Confidence Calibration

'''Definition:''' The alignment between stated confidence and actual accuracy.

'''Audit Procedure:'''
# Sample claims with stated confidence scores
# Verify against primary sources
# Calculate calibration curve
# Identify systematic over/under-confidence

'''Calibration Standards:'''

| Stated Confidence | Expected Accuracy | Tolerance |
|-------------------|-------------------|-----------|
| 0.9-1.0 | 90-100% | ±5% |
| 0.7-0.89 | 70-89% | ±10% |
| 0.5-0.69 | 50-69% | ±15% |
| 0.3-0.49 | 30-49% | ±20% |
| <0.3 | <30% | ±25% |

'''Red Flags:'''
* Confidence >0.9 without primary sources
* Confidence >0.8 without falsification conditions
* All claims by author have confidence >0.85 (overconfidence pattern)
* Confidence never changes despite new evidence

=== 1.2 Source Verification

'''Definition:''' The validity and relevance of cited sources.

'''Audit Procedure:'''
# Extract all citations from content
# Verify source existence and accessibility
# Assess source quality per hierarchy
# Check for citation-context alignment

'''Source Hierarchy Verification:'''

| Tier | Criteria | Verification Method |
|------|----------|---------------------|
| T1 | Primary sources, raw data | Direct access verification |
| T2 | Peer-reviewed research | DOI/citation verification |
| T3 | Expert synthesis | Author credential verification |
| T4 | Secondary sources | Cross-reference verification |
| T5 | Tertiary sources | Multiple source comparison |

'''Red Flags:'''
* T4/T5 sources cited for empirical claims
* Circular citations (A cites B cites A)
* Dead links without archival alternatives
* Sources that don't support cited claims

=== 1.3 Falsification Conditions

'''Definition:''' Explicit conditions under which claims would be proven false.

'''Audit Procedure:'''
# Identify all empirical claims
# Check for falsification conditions
# Assess testability
# Verify prediction track record

'''Falsification Standards:'''

| Claim Type | Required Falsification |
|------------|------------------------|
| Empirical | Specific observation that would disprove |
| Theoretical | Logical contradiction or failed prediction |
| Historical | Documentary evidence contradicting |
| Mathematical | Counter-example or proof of contradiction |

'''Red Flags:'''
* No falsification conditions stated
* Falsification conditions are impossible (e.g., "if logic fails")
* Moving goalposts (conditions change when tested)
* Unfalsifiable claims presented as fact

=== 1.4 Bias Detection

'''Definition:''' Systematic deviation from accuracy due to cognitive or structural factors.

'''Audit Procedure:'''
# Analyze content for bias indicators
# Check author contribution patterns
# Assess topic coverage balance
# Evaluate framing and language

'''Bias Indicators:'''

| Type | Indicator | Detection Method |
|------|-----------|------------------|
| Confirmation | Only supporting evidence cited | Citation balance analysis |
| Availability | Recent/salient events overweighted | Temporal distribution check |
| Authority | Credential-based over evidence-based | Source quality vs. claim strength |
| Selection | Cherry-picked data | Full dataset verification |
| Framing | Loaded language | Linguistic analysis |

'''Red Flags:'''
* Only one perspective represented
* Opposing views straw-manned
* Emotional language for contested claims
* Absence of uncertainty markers

----
== 2. Audit Protocols

=== 2.1 Random Sampling Audit

'''Purpose:''' General quality assessment across corpus.

'''Procedure:'''
# Randomly select 5% of pages
# Apply all four audit dimensions
# Score each page 0-4 per dimension
# Aggregate and analyze patterns

'''Scoring:'''
* 4: Exceeds standards
* 3: Meets standards
* 2: Minor issues
* 1: Major issues
* 0: Critical failures

=== 2.2 Targeted Audit

'''Purpose:''' Deep assessment of specific content areas.

'''Triggers:'''
* High-traffic pages
* Contested content
* Recent major edits
* User reports

'''Procedure:'''
# Select target pages
# Apply intensive audit (all dimensions)
# Document specific issues
# Recommend remediation

=== 2.3 Author Audit

'''Purpose:''' Assess individual contributor patterns.

'''Procedure:'''
# Select author contribution sample
# Analyze confidence calibration
# Check source quality patterns
# Assess bias indicators

'''Privacy Note:''' Author audits are for quality improvement, not punishment. Focus on patterns, not individual errors.

=== 2.4 Temporal Audit

'''Purpose:''' Track quality changes over time.

'''Procedure:'''
# Select pages with 6+ months history
# Compare current vs. historical versions
# Assess epistemic status changes
# Evaluate confidence calibration trends

----
== 3. Audit Tools

=== 3.1 SMW Queries for Audit

'''High-confidence claims without sources:'''
```mediawiki
{{#ask: [[Has confidence::>0.8]] [[Has source count::0]]
|?Has title
|?Has confidence
|format=table
}}
```

'''Claims without falsification conditions:'''
```mediawiki
{{#ask: [[Has falsification conditions::""]] [[Has epistemic status::Established]]
|?Has title
|format=ul
}}
```

'''Authors with calibration concerns:'''
```mediawiki
{{#ask: [[Has author::+]]
|?Has author
|?Has average confidence
|format=table
|sort=Has average confidence
|order=desc
}}
```

=== 3.2 Manual Review Checklist

'''Per-Page Checklist:'''
* [ ] Epistemic status appropriate for evidence
* [ ] Confidence score justified
* [ ] Sources support claims
* [ ] Falsification conditions stated
* [ ] Multiple perspectives represented
* [ ] Uncertainty acknowledged
* [ ] Language neutral where appropriate
* [ ] Provenance complete

'''Per-Author Checklist:'''
* [ ] Confidence calibration reasonable
* [ ] Source quality consistent
* [ ] Bias patterns absent
* [ ] Responsive to feedback
* [ ] Epistemic humility demonstrated

=== 3.3 Automated Checks

'''Script: Epistemic Auditor (Pseudocode)'''
```python
def audit_page(page):
    issues = []
    
    # Confidence check
    if page.confidence > 0.9 and page.source_count < 3:
        issues.append("High confidence with few sources")
    
    # Falsification check
    if page.epistemic_status == "Established" and not page.falsification_conditions:
        issues.append("Established claim without falsification conditions")
    
    # Source check
    if page.primary_sources == 0 and page.epistemic_status in ["Established", "Axiomatic"]:
        issues.append("Strong epistemic status without primary sources")
    
    # Bias check
    if page.perspective_count == 1 and page.epistemic_status == "Contested":
        issues.append("Single perspective on contested topic")
    
    return issues
```

----
== 4. Remediation Protocols

=== 4.1 Minor Issues (Score 2)

'''Action:''' Suggest improvements via talk page.

'''Template:'''
```
Epistemic Audit Note:
- Issue: [Description]
- Standard: [Relevant standard]
- Suggestion: [Specific improvement]
- Priority: Low
```

=== 4.2 Major Issues (Score 1)

'''Action:''' Flag for review, notify author.

'''Template:'''
```
Epistemic Audit Flag:
- Issue: [Description]
- Standard: [Relevant standard]
- Required Action: [Specific fix]
- Timeline: 7 days
- Priority: Medium
```

=== 4.3 Critical Failures (Score 0)

'''Action:''' Immediate review, potential content removal.

'''Template:'''
```
Epistemic Audit Critical:
- Issue: [Description]
- Standard: [Relevant standard]
- Immediate Action: [Specific action]
- Review Required: Yes
- Priority: High
```

=== 4.4 Pattern Remediation

'''Author-Level Issues:'''
# Private communication with author
# Specific examples provided
# Resources for improvement shared
# Follow-up audit scheduled

'''System-Level Issues:'''
# Template/guideline updates
# Training documentation
# Process improvements
# Community discussion

----
== 5. Audit Reporting

=== 5.1 Individual Reports

'''Per-Page Report:'''
```markdown
# Epistemic Audit: [Page Title]
**Date:** [Audit Date]
**Auditor:** [Auditor Name]
**Overall Score:** [0-4]

## Dimension Scores
- Confidence Calibration: [0-4]
- Source Verification: [0-4]
- Falsification Conditions: [0-4]
- Bias Detection: [0-4]

## Findings
[Specific findings]

## Recommendations
[Actionable recommendations]

## Follow-up
[Timeline and responsible party]
```

=== 5.2 Aggregate Reports

'''Quarterly Audit Summary:'''
```markdown
# BITwiki Epistemic Audit: Q1 2026
**Pages Audited:** [N]
**Average Score:** [0-4]
**Critical Issues:** [N]
**Major Issues:** [N]
**Minor Issues:** [N]

## Trends
[Improvement/decline patterns]

## Common Issues
[Most frequent findings]

## Recommendations
[System-level improvements]
```

----
== 6. Continuous Improvement

=== 6.1 Calibration Feedback
* Track auditor calibration
* Compare auditor assessments
* Adjust standards based on evidence
* Update procedures quarterly

=== 6.2 Standard Evolution
* Review standards annually
* Incorporate new research
* Adapt to platform changes
* Community input integration

=== 6.3 Training
* New auditor onboarding
* Calibration exercises
* Bias recognition training
* Tool proficiency

----
== Conclusion

Epistemic audit ensures BITwiki maintains rigorous knowledge standards. Systematic assessment prevents quality drift and maintains community trust.

'''Key Principles:'''
* Audit for improvement, not punishment
* Focus on patterns, not isolated errors
* Balance automation and human judgment
* Evolve standards with evidence

'''Next Steps:'''
# Deploy audit tools
# Train initial auditor cohort
# Conduct baseline assessment
# Establish regular audit schedule

=== 3.2 Manual Review Checklist

'''Per-Page Checklist:'''
* [ ] Epistemic status appropriate for evidence
* [ ] Confidence score justified
* [ ] Sources support claims
* [ ] Falsification conditions stated
* [ ] Multiple perspectives represented
* [ ] Uncertainty acknowledged
* [ ] Language neutral where appropriate
* [ ] Provenance complete

'''Per-Author Checklist:'''
* [ ] Confidence calibration reasonable

* [ ] Bias patterns absent
* [ ] Responsive to feedback
* [ ] Epistemic humility demonstrated

=== 3.3 Automated Checks

'''Script: Epistemic Auditor (Pseudocode)'''
```python
def audit_page(page):
    issues = []
    
    # Confidence check
    if page.confidence > 0.9 and page.source_count < 3:
        issues.append("High confidence with few sources")
    
    # Falsification check
    if page.epistemic_status == "Established" and not page.falsification_conditions:
        issues.append("Established claim without falsification conditions")
    
    # Source check
    if page.primary_sources == 0 and page.epistemic_status in ["Established", "Axiomatic"]:
        issues.append("Strong epistemic status without primary sources")
    
    # Bias check
    if page.perspective_count == 1 and page.epistemic_status == "Contested":
        issues.append("Single perspective on contested topic")
    
    return issues
```
